correctness.rationale: The proposed 60-vertex polytope and all 32 facet normals are derived in the checker from the exact icosahedral edge graph. All active facets are verified by exact algebraic inequalities. The 16-line affine arrangement has exactly 84 regions, independently established by the Euler intersection formula, and 84 distinct sign regions are constructed, proving exhaustiveness. Across both hemispheres there are 152 regions with 20 or 21 illuminated vertices, never more than 21. Each of 20 explicit face-opposing directions illuminates 21 vertices; each vertex is illuminated by 7. Weight 1/7 per direction proves the upper fractional bound; summing the 60 vertex constraints and 21-per-direction bound proves the lower fractional bound. Nongeneric directions preserve all strictly illuminated vertices under small generic perturbations. The complete standalone verifier was executed on its actual package code path.

originality.rationale: Neither the foundational 2009 fractional theory nor the 2026 sharp universal theorem computes the truncated-icosahedral value. A published exact evaluation for the icosahedron and dodecahedron uses a matching symmetry idea but requires different, independently computed vertex-incidence maxima. The 2012 full text supplies an ordinary four-light-source upper bound for the truncated icosahedron in a distinct quantitative illumination study, but does not give fractional value 20/7 or the 21-of-60 incidence certificate. Exact source, parameter and alias searches did not locate an implication-equivalent determination. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The regular truncated icosahedron is the canonical Archimedean 60-vertex truncation, and its exact fractional illumination is a natural finite-dimensional convex-geometric invariant. The nonintegral value 20/7 and sharp 7/5 ordinary/fractional gap are a complete exact determination not provided by universal inequalities or the previously known four-source ordinary cover. The 152-cell exact certificate is a reusable sharp normal-fan method, and twenty symmetric directions make the fractionally optimal measure transparent.
